record.context_brief: Continuous inverse subspace for the Hausdorff moment operator
record.original_question: Let B^(H): L2(0,1) -> l2 be the Hausdorff moment operator defined by [B^(H) z]_j = integral_0^1 t^(j-1) z(t) dt for j = 1, 2, .... The inverse problem B^(H) z = y is known to be ill-posed of type I, and there exists an infinite-dimensional subspace of the data space l2 on which the inverse of B^(H) is continuous. Which infinite-dimensional subspace is it?

evidence.quote: In the recent paper [4], we have dealt with properties of the forward operator B (H) : L2 (0, 1) -> l2 of the Hausdorff moment problem defined as [B (H) z]j := integral_0^1 t^(j-1) z(t)dt (j = 1, 2, ...).

This means that there is an infinite dimensional subspace of l2 on which the inverse of B (H) is continuous. Despite considerable efforts in [4], a full description of this subspace is still missing. Open Question 1: What is the infinite dimensional subspace of l2 , on which the inverse of the operator B (H) is continuous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Hausdorff moment operator
\[ B^{(H)}: L^2(0,1) \to \ell^2, \qquad [B^{(H)} z]_j := \int_0^1 t^{j-1} z(t)\, dt, \qquad j = 1, 2, \dots \]
This operator is bounded, injective and has non-closed range, so the equation $B^{(H)} z = y$ is ill-posed; moreover it is ill-posed of type I in the sense of Nashed, meaning that there exists an infinite-dimensional closed subspace $V \subset \ell^2$ such that the restriction of $(B^{(H)})^{-1}$ to $V \cap \mathrm{range}(B^{(H)})$ is continuous.

Problem: Give an explicit, full description of an infinite-dimensional subspace $V$ of $\ell^2$ on which the inverse of $B^{(H)}$ is continuous.
artifact.category_tag: Hausdorff moment problem and ill-posed inverse problems
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal that the Hausdorff moment operator on L^2(0,1) is a well-known example of a non-compact, ill-posed-of-type-I linear operator, and follow-up works (e.g., on degree of ill-posedness via the spectral theorem and on compositions of non-compact operators) continue to investigate its stability properties without giving a full description of an infinite-dimensional subspace of l^2 on which its inverse is continuous. No source found provides an explicit complete characterization of such a subspace, so the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Hausdorff Moment Problem in the light of ill-posedness of type I
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes that the Hausdorff moment operator is non-compact and the corresponding inverse problem is ill-posed of type I, implying existence of an infinite-dimensional stability subspace, without a full description.
status_evidence.claim: Background paper establishing the type-I ill-posedness but not characterizing the stability subspace.

status_evidence.title: A unified concept of the degree of ill-posedness ... (2408.01148)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work re-examining the Hausdorff moment operator's degree of ill-posedness via the spectral theorem, indicating ongoing study of its stability structure.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature still treats the Hausdorff moment operator's stability properties as an active topic.

status_evidence.title: Curious ill-posedness phenomena in the composition of non-compact linear operators
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses non-compact Hausdorff-type operators and their compositions, without supplying a full description of an infinite-dimensional subspace of l^2 on which the inverse is continuous.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit resolution of the open question is reported in this later work.
